task_description: Designing and selecting high-performing binary electrolyte additive combinations for LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO)-based lithium-ion batteries by predicting three key electrochemical performance metrics: final area-specific impedance (ASI), impedance rise (ΔASI), and final specific capacity (Q), with the goal of identifying formulations that simultaneously minimize ASI and ΔASI while maximizing Q.

datasets.db_description: A custom experimental dataset comprising electrochemical performance measurements from 28 electrolyte formulations tested in Gr||LNMO coin cells, including 10 single additives and 18 dual additives (each composed of one positive-electrode and one negative-electrode additive), plus a baseline solvent (1.0 M LiPF6 in EC/EMC). For each formulation, the dataset contains measured values of final area-specific impedance (ASI), impedance rise (ΔASI), and final specific capacity (Q), along with corresponding chemical compositions (e.g., '1% VC + 1% TMSPi') and weight percentages. This dataset was used to train and validate Gaussian Process Regression models to predict ASI, ΔASI, and Q for unseen dual-additive candidates.
